The profile likelihood [@raue2009structural] shows how well the data constrain each parameter.
This chapter profiles the full model at the best fit of [Optimization](guide-optimization.html),
tests the core model of the publication and fits a reduced model.

## Profile likelihood and confidence intervals

The profile of a parameter is the data term along the path on which the other parameters minimize
the objective with that parameter fixed. Here the objective has a prior of standard deviation 20
on the log scale at the best fit, so that the data term shapes the profiles. Data terms within
3.84, the 95 % quantile of $\chi^2_1$, of the minimum form the 95 % confidence interval
([Methods > Profile likelihood](methods-profiles.html)). `stepControl = list(stop = "data")` ends a
profile there, `confint(val.column = "data")` reads the interval, `profileThreshold()` gives other
levels. A profile open towards $-\infty$ means the process can be switched off, towards
$+\infty$ that it can be instantaneous ([Methods > Shapes](methods-profiles.html#shapes)).

`method = "integrate"` (default) follows the constrained optimum as a curve, with
`algoControl = list(reoptimize = TRUE)` corrected by `trust()`; `method = "optimize"` refits at
every step.

| entry of `stepControl` | `"integrate"` | `"optimize"` | controls |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stepsize` | `1e-4` | `1e-2` | first step |
| `min`, `max` | `1e-4`, `Inf` | `1e-4`, `Inf` | bounds of the step |
| `atol`, `rtol` | `1e-2` | `1e-1` | mismatch of predicted and actual change |
| `limit` | `500` | `100` | steps per side |
| `stop` | `"value"` | `"value"` | part of the objective compared with the threshold |

`limits` bounds the profiled parameter, `side` profiles one side, `cores` profiles in parallel
([Remote computing](guide-remote-computing.html#threads-and-processes)).

## Profiles of the full model

`profiles.R` refits the best fit of the multistart to the tolerances of the profiles,

```{r refit, eval = FALSE}
```

fits the objective of the profiles once,

```{r profileprior, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/fits.rds", "fit.R"))
invisible(stored("results/profiles.rds", "profiles.R"))
```

and profiles each side until the data term has risen by the threshold or the parameter has moved
by 7. The profiles are loaded from `results/profiles.rds`:

```{r profiles, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
saved <- readRDS("results/profiles.rds")
refit <- saved$refit
fitProfile <- saved$fitProfile
profiles <- saved$profiles
```

The data term at the refit and at the optimum of the profiles:

```{r}
dataTerm <- function(p) attr(obj(p, fixed = gauge), "data")
c(refit = dataTerm(refit$argument), profiles = dataTerm(fitProfile$argument))
```

Without the prior of `model.R` the data term falls by
`r round(dataTerm(refit$argument) - dataTerm(fitProfile$argument), 2)`. No profile lies below the
fit:

```{r}
c(fit = fitProfile$value, lowest = min(profiles$value))
```

```{r}
intervals <- confint(profiles, level = 0.95, val.column = "data")
intervals$shape <- with(intervals, ifelse(is.finite(lower) & is.finite(upper), "finite",
                       ifelse(is.finite(lower), "open above",
                              ifelse(is.finite(upper), "open below", "open on both sides"))))
table(intervals$shape)
rownames(intervals) <- NULL
intervals[intervals$shape != "finite", c("name", "value", "lower", "upper", "shape")]
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# the largest rise of the prior on an open side, against the prior at the optimum
along <- as.data.frame(profiles)
openSides <- intervals[intervals$shape != "finite", ]
priorRise <- max(mapply(function(name, shape) {
  d <- along[along$whichPar == name, ]
  side <- switch(shape, "open above" = d$constraint >= 0, "open below" = d$constraint <= 0, TRUE)
  max(d$prior[side] - d$prior[which.min(abs(d$constraint))])
}, openSides$name, openSides$shape))
```

The open profiles; on an open side the prior rises by up to `r ceiling(10 * priorRise) / 10`:

```{r}
# panels wide enough for the parameter names, few ticks and the legend below
readable <- list(ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3)),
                 ggplot2::guides(x = ggplot2::guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE)),
                 ggplot2::theme(strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
                                panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(1.5, "lines"), legend.position = "bottom"),
                 ggplot2::labs(x = "log value", color = NULL, linetype = NULL))
```

```{r, fig.height = 11}
open <- intervals$name[intervals$shape != "finite"]
plotProfile(profiles, mode %in% c("data", "prior"), name %in% open, ncol = 4) + readable
```

## Parameter paths

`plotPaths()` shows how the other parameters compensate along a profile. Along `act_Ikb_Base`,
`eta_act_Ikb_Base_c_pNfkIkb` rises by the same amount: the data determine the product. Shown are
the parameters that move by more than 1:

```{r, fig.height = 4}
# the parameters that move along the profile of `par` by more than `by` on the log scale
movers <- function(par, by = 1) {
  d <- as.data.frame(profiles)[profiles$whichPar == par, ]
  others <- setdiff(names(fitProfile$argument), par)
  others[vapply(d[others], function(v) diff(range(v)) > by, NA)]
}
for (par in c("act_Ikb_Base", "int_Nfk"))
  print(plotPaths(profiles, partner %in% movers(par), whichPar = par) +
          ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(partner), ncol = 4) +
          ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3)) +
          ggplot2::theme(strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9)) +
          ggplot2::labs(x = paste("change of", par), y = "change of the parameter"))
```

## Predictions along a profile

`plotArray()` predicts along one side of a profile, colored by the profiled parameter; `fixed`
adds the gauge. Along the upper side of `degrad_RnaA20`, `RnaA20` falls by two orders of magnitude
while A20 stays nearly the same:

```{r, fig.height = 5}
states <- x * pSS * p
minutes <- seq(0, 360, 2)
chain <- c("RnaA20_1", "RnaA20_2", "RnaA20", "A20")
plotArray("degrad_RnaA20", profiles, states, minutes, name %in% chain, condition == "TNF",
          direction = "up", nSim = 5, fixed = gauge)
```

Along the lower side of `ext_nNfkIkb` the nuclear complex builds up at the expense of free and
phosphorylated nuclear NFκB; their sum, read out by nucNFkB, stays the same:

```{r, fig.height = 5}
plotArray("ext_nNfkIkb", profiles, states, minutes, name %in% c("nNfk", "pnNfk", "nNfkIkb"),
          condition == "TNF", direction = "down", nSim = 5, fixed = gauge)
```

## Core model of the publication

The core model of the publication has 29 reactions [@oppelt2018model, Table S5] and fixed values
(Tables S8 and S9), on the log scale:

| setting of the core model | parameter of the full model | value |
|---|---|---|
| IKK activated by the receptors only: no basal activation | `act_Ikk_Base` | $-\infty$ |
| no inhibition of IKK by A20 | `inh_Ikk` | $\infty$ |
| basal phosphorylation of IκBα only in the complex with pNFκB, at a rate `act_Ikb_complex` | `act_Ikb_Base` | $-\infty$ |
| IκBα phosphorylated by pIKK in the complexes with NFκB and pNFκB at the same rate | `eta_act_Ikb_c_pNfkIkb` | 0 |
| NFκB phosphorylated by pIKK only | `act_Nfk_Base` | $-\infty$ |
| ppIKK phosphorylates neither IκBα nor NFκB | `eta_s_ppIkk` | $-\infty$ |
| pNFκB released without a separate factor, at `split_NfkIkb` | `eta_split_pNfkpIkb` | 0 |
| slow receptor deactivation, 0.001 per minute | `deact_TNFR` | $\ln 10^{-3}$ |
| slow import of NFκB, 0.01 per minute | `int_Nfk` | $\ln 10^{-2}$ |
| fast dephosphorylation of nuclear pNFκB, 1000 per minute | `deact_pnNfk` | $\ln 10^{3}$ |
| fast formation of the nuclear complex, 1000 per minute | `eta_form_complex_nuc` | $\ln 10^{3}$ minus `form_complex` |
| fast export of the complex, 1000 per minute | `ext_nNfkIkb` | $\ln 10^{3}$ |
| no offset of the IκBα blots, no bleaching of A20-GFP | `off_IkBa`, `off_ipIkBa_ibIkBa`, `tau_A20GFP` | $-\infty$ |
| one delay step of the A20 transcript instead of two | none | |

Against the intervals of the full model:

```{r}
core <- c(act_Ikk_Base = -Inf, inh_Ikk = Inf, act_Ikb_Base = -Inf, eta_act_Ikb_c_pNfkIkb = 0,
          act_Nfk_Base = -Inf, eta_s_ppIkk = -Inf, eta_split_pNfkpIkb = 0,
          deact_TNFR = log(1e-3), int_Nfk = log(1e-2), deact_pnNfk = log(1000),
          eta_form_complex_nuc = log(1000) - fitProfile$argument[["form_complex"]],
          ext_nNfkIkb = log(1000), off_IkBa = -Inf, off_ipIkBa_ibIkBa = -Inf, tau_A20GFP = -Inf)
settings <- intervals[match(names(core), intervals$name), c("name", "lower", "upper", "shape")]
settings$core <- core
settings$inside <- with(settings, core >= lower & core <= upper)
rownames(settings) <- NULL
settings
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
deact <- settings[settings$name == "deact_pnNfk", ]
```

Every setting but one lies in the 95 % interval; the data bound `deact_pnNfk` to
`r signif(exp(deact$lower), 2)` to `r signif(exp(deact$upper), 2)` per minute, below the fixed
1000. No profile tests the single delay step, and the publication gives no reason for it. The
likelihood ratio test takes all settings together: `variants.R` fits the core model and the variants that release one setting, loaded from
`results/variants.rds`:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/variants.rds", "variants.R"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
variants <- readRDS("results/variants.rds")
reducedRatio <- readRDS("results/reduced.rds")$ratio
released <- c(delays = "two delay steps of the A20 transcript", split = "separate factor `eta_split_pNfkpIkb`",
              setNames(paste0("`", rownames(variants)[-(1:3)], "` estimated"), rownames(variants)[-(1:3)]))
coreData <- variants["core", "data"]
bothLower <- coreData - (reducedRatio[["reduced"]])
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
shown <- variants[-1, ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(released = released[rownames(shown)],
                        `lower by` = round(coreData - shown[, "data"], 2),
                        `above full` = round(shown[, "difference"], 2),
                        threshold = round(shown[, "threshold"], 2), check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE)
```

The core model lies `r round(variants["core", "difference"], 2)` above the full model, against
the threshold `r round(variants["core", "threshold"], 2)` for
`r variants["core", "removed"]` removed parameters, and is
`r if (variants["core", "difference"] < variants["core", "threshold"]) "accepted" else "rejected"`.
The two delay steps and the separate factor together lower the data term by
`r round(bothLower, 2)` at one added parameter, more than 3.84; `reduced.R` takes both and sets the
scale `s_ipNFkB_ibNFkB`, whose profile is open below, to 0.

## Reduced model

The core model with two delay steps, the separate factor and the scale `s_ipNFkB_ibNFkB` at 0:

```{r reducedreactions, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r reducedobservables, eval = FALSE}
```

As in the publication, all NFκB rests in the complex with IκBα and all IKK is inactive, a steady
state for every parameter value, so neither `Pimpl()` nor a stability term is needed:




```{r}
saved <- readRDS("results/reduced.rds")
saved$ratio
```

## Profiles of the reduced model

With the prior and settings of the profiles of the full model:

```{r reducedprofileprior, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r reducedprofiles, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
intervalsReduced <- confint(saved$profiles, level = 0.95, val.column = "data")
intervalsReduced$shape <- with(intervalsReduced, ifelse(is.finite(lower) & is.finite(upper), "finite",
                              ifelse(is.finite(lower), "open above",
                                     ifelse(is.finite(upper), "open below", "open on both sides"))))
rownames(intervalsReduced) <- NULL
table(intervalsReduced$shape)
intervalsReduced[intervalsReduced$shape != "finite", c("name", "value", "lower", "upper", "shape")]
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# the rise of the data term at the upper end of the profile of complex formation
fc <- as.data.frame(saved$profiles)
fc <- fc[fc$whichPar == "form_complex", ]
plateau <- fc$data[which.max(fc$constraint)] - fc$data[fc$constraint == 0][1]
fcLower <- intervalsReduced$lower[intervalsReduced$name == "form_complex"] / log(10)
```

All parameters are identifiable except `form_complex`, bounded below at
`r signif(fcLower, 2)` on the log10 scale and open above on a plateau `r round(plateau, 2)` above
the optimum; the publication reports (-0.21, 3.03). The profiles of `degrad_A20`,
`degrad_RnaA20` and `shuttle_RnaA20` have a second minimum inside the interval. The rate constants:

```{r}
rates <- setdiff(intervalsReduced$name, grep("^(s|off|sigma|tau)_", intervalsReduced$name, value = TRUE))
intervalsReduced[intervalsReduced$name %in% rates, c("name", "value", "lower", "upper")]
```

```{r, fig.height = 11}
plotProfile(saved$profiles, mode %in% c("data", "prior"), name %in% rates, ncol = 4) + readable
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
along <- as.data.frame(saved$profiles)
optimum <- saved$fitProfile$argument
# the fits of the multistart within 0.001 of the best, by side of the fixed set of the swap
fits <- as.data.frame(saved$fits)
best <- fits[fits$value < min(fits$value) + 1e-3, ]
below <- sum(best$degrad_A20 < best$degrad_RnaA20)
# the point of the profile of degrad_RnaA20 at the mirror image of the optimum
rna <- along[along$whichPar == "degrad_RnaA20", ]
mirror <- rna[which.min(abs(rna$degrad_RnaA20 - optimum[["degrad_A20"]])), ]
# the first local minimum of the lower side of the profile of shuttle_RnaA20, away from the optimum
shuttle <- along[along$whichPar == "shuttle_RnaA20" &
                   along$shuttle_RnaA20 < optimum[["shuttle_RnaA20"]] - 0.5, ]
shuttle <- shuttle[order(shuttle$shuttle_RnaA20), ]
second <- shuttle[which(diff(sign(diff(shuttle$data))) > 0)[1] + 1, ]
# the fits of the multistart at that point
atSecond <- sum(abs(fits$shuttle_RnaA20 - second$shuttle_RnaA20) < 0.1 &
                  abs(fits$degrad_A20 - fits$degrad_RnaA20) < 0.1)
```

Exchanging `degrad_A20` and `degrad_RnaA20` leaves every readout and the prior unchanged, a
discrete symmetry ([Symmetries > Discrete symmetries](guide-symmetries.html#discrete-symmetries)).
Of the `r nrow(best)` best fits of the multistart, `r below` lie on the side
`degrad_A20 < degrad_RnaA20` and `r nrow(best) - below` at the mirror image. The profile of
`degrad_RnaA20` passes through the mirror image of the optimum, within
`r format(signif(mirror$data - min(along$data), 1), scientific = FALSE)`
of the data term at the optimum.

The second minimum of `shuttle_RnaA20` is another local optimum, close to the fixed set of the
swap: at `shuttle_RnaA20` = `r round(second$shuttle_RnaA20, 2)` the degradation rates are
`r round(second$degrad_A20, 2)` and `r round(second$degrad_RnaA20, 2)`, the data term
`r round(second$data - min(along$data), 2)` above the optimum, reached by `r atSecond` fits of the
multistart. The estimates of the publication, $-4.72$ and $-4.46$ [@oppelt2018model, Table S7],
also lie close to the fixed set.

## Profiles in the fundamental domain

The fundamental domain `degrad_A20 < degrad_RnaA20` holds the optimum and removes the swap.
`fundamental.R` fits the reduced model in the chart that
`symmetryReduction(branch = "degrad_A20 < degrad_RnaA20")` returns, with
`define("degrad_RnaA20 <- degrad_A20 + delta_RnaA20")` before `insert("x <- exp(x)")`; the fixed
set lies at `delta_RnaA20` $\to -\infty$. Only the parameter transformation is new:

```{r fundamentaltrafo, eval = FALSE}
```

`delta_RnaA20` has the prior of `degrad_RnaA20`, mean $\log(1/60)$ and standard deviation 2:

```{r fundamentalobjective, eval = FALSE}
```

One fit from the best fit of `refit.R`, loaded with the profiles from `results/fundamental.rds`:

```{r fundamentalfit, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
invisible(stored("results/fundamental.rds", "fundamental.R"))
```

```{r}
fundamental <- readRDS("results/fundamental.rds")
fundamental$dataTerms
```

Profiles with the prior and settings of the reduced model:

```{r fundamentalprofileprior, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r fundamentalprofiles, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
c(reduced = saved$fitProfile$value, fundamental = fundamental$fitProfile$value)
intervalsFundamental <- confint(fundamental$profiles, level = 0.95, val.column = "data")
rownames(intervalsFundamental) <- NULL
swapped <- c("degrad_A20", "delta_RnaA20", "shuttle_RnaA20")
intervalsFundamental[intervalsFundamental$name %in% swapped, c("name", "value", "lower", "upper")]
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
alongFundamental <- as.data.frame(fundamental$profiles)
# the data term at the lower end of the profile of delta_RnaA20, against the optimum
delta <- alongFundamental[alongFundamental$whichPar == "delta_RnaA20", ]
edge <- delta[which.min(delta$delta_RnaA20), ]
plateauDelta <- edge$data - min(alongFundamental$data)
upperA20 <- intervalsFundamental$upper[intervalsFundamental$name == "degrad_A20"]
upperA20Reduced <- intervalsReduced$upper[intervalsReduced$name == "degrad_A20"]
# the largest change of an interval bound of another parameter
both <- merge(intervalsFundamental, intervalsReduced, by = "name")
both <- both[!both$name %in% swapped, ]
moved <- max(abs(c(both$lower.x - both$lower.y, both$upper.x - both$upper.y)), na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r, fig.height = 11}
ratesFundamental <- setdiff(intervalsFundamental$name,
                            grep("^(s|off|sigma|tau)_", intervalsFundamental$name, value = TRUE))
plotProfile(fundamental$profiles, mode %in% c("data", "prior"), name %in% ratesFundamental,
            ncol = 4) + readable
```

No profile crosses into the mirror image. The profile of `delta_RnaA20` is open below, leveling
off `r round(plateauDelta, 2)` above the optimum at the fixed set. The upper bound of `degrad_A20`
falls from `r round(upperA20Reduced, 2)` to `r round(upperA20, 2)`; the other intervals change by
at most `r format(signif(moved, 1), scientific = FALSE)`.
